Add comorbidity indicators and scores (experimental)

Source: R/comorbidity.R
nis_comorbidity.Rd

DuckDB unpivots diagnosis slots, maps codes to conditions, and applies present-on-admission and hierarchy rules within each discharge. Lazy queries stay in DuckDB. The function runs a key and diagnosis-availability check before returning the score query. Collected data frames keep their row order.

Usage

nis_comorbidity(.data, method = "elixhauser_ahrq_icd10", prefix = "cmrb_")

Arguments

.data

A data frame, a tbl_svy from nis_design(), or a lazy DuckDB query. Lazy input requires non-missing, unique KEY_NIS, or unique pairs of YEAR and KEY_NIS when YEAR is present. Keep YEAR when pooling years.

method

Comorbidity definition. The default "elixhauser_ahrq_icd10" uses the medicalcoder ICD-10-CM union. "elixhauser_ahrq2022" through "elixhauser_ahrq2027" select a specific release. Use "charlson_quan2005" for Quan coding with original Charlson weights, "charlson_quan2011" for the same coding with Quan 2011 weights, and "charlson_deyo1992" for Deyo ICD-9-CM coding with original weights. "elixhauser_quan2005" uses Quan ICD-9-CM or ICD-10 coding and legacy AHRQ weights. "elixhauser_ahrq_web" and "elixhauser_elixhauser1998" replicate medicalcoder's legacy ICD-9 code-based algorithms. All methods except FY2027 require the optional medicalcoder package.

prefix

Prefix for the added columns. Choose a prefix that does not collide with an existing name.

Value

.data with logical condition flags and <prefix>any, the integer count <prefix>n, and either <prefix>mortality_index and <prefix>readmission_index (Elixhauser) or <prefix>cci (Charlson). Charlson scores are based on diagnoses and any mapped procedures without an age adjustment.

Coding and present on admission

  • Use ICD-10-CM I10_DX* or ICD-9-CM DX* slots as supported by the method. The first slot identifies the principal diagnosis and is excluded from flags. When supplied, YEAR, DQTR and DXVER identify eligible diagnosis slots. Deyo also reads eligible ICD-9-CM PR* slots when available and mapped. Keep ICD-9 codes as strings to retain leading zeros.

  • Codes use uppercase with periods and ASCII whitespace removed. Rows with usable codes that map to no conditions receive zeros. Rows without usable codes for the method receive missing scores and trigger a warning.

  • Refined AHRQ and Charlson align DXPOAn to the diagnosis suffix n. Y and W mean present, N and U mean absent, and other values including 1 mean unknown. Refined AHRQ also uses code-specific exemptions. For methods sourced from medicalcoder, repeated diagnoses that map to the same category and exemption state follow its data.frame precedence (unknown, then present, then absent).

  • If a matching POA field is absent, easyNIS warns and assumes those diagnoses were present. NIS releases generally lack POA indicators, so this assumption can count conditions acquired during a hospital stay. AHRQ's software leaves 18 of 38 measures unset when POA is unavailable.

  • elixhauser_ahrq2027 selects its exemption list using the discharge fiscal year (calendar YEAR plus one for DQTR == 4). When the quarter is missing it uses the calendar year. When the year is missing or after the release, it uses the latest fiscal year in the release. The other refined methods use medicalcoder's fixed exemptions.

Use with nis_design()

Retain diagnosis slots and available POA fields using keep, then pass the design to nis_comorbidity(). For a tbl_svy, only the design's variables are enriched. The clusters, strata and weights are preserved.

See also

Comorbidity indicators.

Examples

discharges <- data.frame(I10_DX1 = "Z0000", I10_DX2 = "I509", DXPOA1 = "Y", DXPOA2 = "Y")
nis_comorbidity(discharges, method = "elixhauser_ahrq2027")$cmrb_mortality_index
